WITH sentiment_with_trader AS (
  SELECT sf.transref, t.tradekind, sf.anlycount
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals sf
  INNER JOIN trader t ON sf.trdref2 = t.tradereg
),
pair_averages AS (
  SELECT transref, tradekind, AVG(anlycount) FILTER (WHERE anlycount IS NOT NULL) as avg_anlycount
  FROM sentiment_with_trader
  GROUP BY transref, tradekind
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_anlycount) as mean_avg_anlycount FROM pair_averages
),
kept_pairs AS (
  SELECT pa.transref, pa.tradekind, pa.avg_anlycount, pa.avg_anlycount - om.mean_avg_anlycount as above_mean
  FROM pair_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
  WHERE pa.avg_anlycount > om.mean_avg_anlycount
),
trader_type_stats AS (
  SELECT tradekind, AVG(avg_anlycount) as avg_analyst_count, AVG(above_mean) as avg_above_mean
  FROM kept_pairs
  GROUP BY tradekind
),
trader_type_means AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_analyst_count) as mean_analyst_count FROM trader_type_stats
)
SELECT ts.tradekind, ts.avg_analyst_count, ts.avg_above_mean, ts.avg_analyst_count / ttm.mean_analyst_count
FROM trader_type_stats ts
CROSS JOIN trader_type_means ttm
ORDER BY ts.tradekind

assumptions.assumption: The phrase "this figure" in the final ratio ("average analyst count divided by the mean of this figure across all trader types") refers to "the average analyst count of its kept pairs", yielding: (trader type's avg analyst count) / (mean of all trader types' avg analyst counts).

alternatives.interpretation: "This figure" refers to "their average amount above the overall mean" instead, so the ratio divides the analyst count by the mean of the above-mean amounts across trader types.
